result.note: Tested the venue of Putin's remarks and the CAATSA, Su-57 and tariff facts; the US visa ban anecdote and the analysis on CAATSA losing its teeth were left out.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, Russian President Vladimir Putin warned that any attempt to pressure India through sanctions would "boomerang immediately". At which forum did he say this?
questions.explain: Putin spoke at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum on Friday 5 June 2026, answering questions on whether India risked US sanctions by buying Russian weapons. His speech came while US trade officials were in New Delhi negotiating the first tranche of a bilateral trade deal.
questions.source: Speaking at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum last Friday, Putin declared that any attempt to pressure India through sanctions would "boomerang immediately" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements in the context of Putin's June 2026 remarks on India and US sanctions:
items: The Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA) is a United States law penalising significant transactions with Russia.
India and Russia jointly developed the Su-57 stealth fighter, which Russia is now offering to sell.
The 50% US tariff on Indian goods is partly a penalty for Indian purchases of Russian oil.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. A joint India–Russia development programme for the Su-57 was proposed earlier but never materialised, and Russia now offers the jet for sale. The questions Putin answered concerned CAATSA exposure from buying the Su-57 or the S-500 air defence system.
questions.source: A joint development programme was proposed earlier but never materialised.
